lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: why exponential growth eventually exceeds polynomial growth
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: why exponential growth eventually exceeds polynomial growth

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A population of 600 grows by 2% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 4 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 35 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
A stays ahead permanently because 35 is larger than 2.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 1200(0.94)^t, with t in years. What does 0.94 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $1200
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.94, meaning a 6% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (4, -9) and (6, -13). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 8, 12, 16, 20. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A population of 2800 grows by 2% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 5 years, to the nearest whole number.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
